newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street firms expected to see Q2 profit drop.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street firms expected to see Q2 profit drop.

text.p: Profits at the major Wall Street firms are expected to sag noticeably from the first quarter of 1997 to the second, a view which has been reinforced this week by reports from two firms.
Tuesday, A.G. Edwards Inc said earnings for the fiscal first quarter ended May 31 fell to $0.83 per share from $0.87 a year ago and $0.90 in the February quarter.
Wednesday, Goldman Sachs & Co said pre-tax earnings fell to $610 million in the May quarter from $905 million in the February quarter.

Goldman Sachs, a privately held company and a powerhouse in investment banking, stressed that the first-half earnings of $1.52 billion, combining the February and May quarters, set a record and were up 19 percent from a year ago. Goldman Sachs said all of its business lines were strong.

A source familiar with the situation cautioned against reading too much into the quarter-to-quarter comparison because the $905 million earned in the first fiscal quarter was an "out-of-the-ballpark" number. The $610 million earned in the second quarter was above expectations and respectable, the source said.
